name: orchestration-request-admission
goal: Refuse provider calls that could cross 190000 active context tokens before issuing the request, then preserve checkpoint handoff and fresh restart.

evidence: Use a live process fixture with 138000 observed context and 60000 bytes of pending input. The provider request must be stopped before transport and the checkpoint must resume.

The previous CLI case monitored provider usage after dispatch. The new normal-entry integration fixture submits a second payload below the handoff threshold and verifies pre-request rotation with separate telemetry.
Frozen no-gate fixture failed the checkpoint resume assertion before code changes.
Both provider CLIs route model inputs through the local admission boundary; estimates are stored separately from observed usage.
Unchanged normal-entry regression refused the oversized pending request and completed in a fresh session.
